mainTopic: Which holy animals count as their owner's property, and collecting damages from שלמים
overview: The amud opens by asking why the earlier answer did not simply split the sources between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבנן. The גמרא explains that a בכור is a מתנת כהונה, which the כהנים receive "from the table of the Most High," so it is different. Next the גמרא quotes the full ברייתא on "וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל בַּה׳". רבי יוחנן explains that בן עזאי's narrow wording leaves out מעשר בהמה, which can never be sold. In רבינא's version, the same analysis is placed on אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי's words, and the word "only" there ends in a קשיא. רבא then offers a different reading of the משנה: it means ordinary property of a הדיוט. That reading also meets an unanswered קשיא. Finally, רבי אבא rules that damages caused by שלמים are collected from the meat, not from the אימורין, and the גמרא shows how this ruling fits both רבנן and רבי נתן.

steps.title: Why not split the sources between two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבינא did not answer רבא's objection simply by saying the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and רב נחמן's ruling follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him answer: this source follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, and that one follows רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an easier way to answer the earlier objection: just say the two sources follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that קדשים קלים are the owner's property, so a source that treats them as property can follow him. רב נחמן's ruling, that a בכור may not be sold while the בית המקדש stands, could follow רבנן, who disagree. The גמרא is asking why the earlier answer did not use this simple split.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him answer (why not give this answer?)
The Sages, who disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי

phrases.english: Let him answer: this follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא that treats קדשים קלים as the owner's property.

phrases.english: and that follows the Rabbis!
phrases.notes: "That" is רב נחמן's ruling that a בכור can't be sold while the בית המקדש stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישַׁנֵּי: הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous daf about רבא's objection to רב נחמן's ruling on selling a בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer given earlier to רבא's objection.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler answer seems available: assign the two sources to two different תנאים, רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבנן.

steps.title: Priestly gifts are different
steps.stepSummary: A בכור is a מתנת כהונה, which the כהנים receive from God's table, so even רבי יוסי הגלילי would not treat it like ordinary private property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you talking about gifts to the כהנים? Gifts to the כהנים are different, because when the כהנים receive them, they receive them from the table of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the simple split does not work: a בכור belongs to a special category of gifts for the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי called קדשים קלים "his property" only for offerings a person sets aside himself. A בכור is a gift to the כהן, and the כהן receives it from God's table, not as his own private property. So רבי יוסי הגלילי's view cannot be used to explain a source about a בכור, and the suggested split fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts that belong to the כהנים, such as a בכור
It is different
They receive / gain ownership
The table of the Most High (God's table)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying a בכור is not one of the קדשים קלים. It still is; the point is that its ownership works differently because it is a gift to the כהנים.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that כהנים receive their gifts "from the table of the Most High" explains why their portions are not treated like ordinary private property.

phrases.english: (He said to him:) Are you speaking of gifts of the priesthood?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: Gifts of the priesthood are different,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי קָא זָכוּ – מִשֻּׁלְחַן גָּבוֹהַּ קָא זָכוּ.
phrases.english: for when they receive them, they receive them from the table of the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה קָאָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the simple answer suggested in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between categories (ordinary קדשים קלים compared with priestly gifts)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule about קדשים קלים being property should apply to a בכור too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בכור is a priestly gift received from God's table, so even רבי יוסי הגלילי does not treat it as the owner's ordinary property.

steps.title: The ברייתא itself: three views on "וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל בַּה׳"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the full ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the פסוק includes קדשים קלים, בן עזאי says it includes שלמים, and אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says בן עזאי meant only a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the ברייתא itself: "And commits a trespass against ה׳" comes to include קדשים קלים, which are the owner's property. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי. בן עזאי says: it comes to include שלמים. אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says: בן עזאי said this only about a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the full ברייתא that was mentioned earlier so it can study it carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of someone who denies holding his friend's property and swears falsely. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads it to include קדשים קלים because they are the owner's money. בן עזאי includes שלמים, and אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי reports that בן עזאי actually spoke only about a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא now studies the source it quoted earlier
"And commits a trespass against ה׳‎" (ויקרא 5:21)
Offerings of lesser holiness
Peace offerings
A firstborn animal, given to the כהן

phrases.english: The matter itself: "And commits a trespass against the Lord"
comes to include offerings of lesser sanctity, which are his property,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַשְּׁלָמִים.
phrases.english: Ben Azzai says: to include peace-offerings.
Abba Yosei ben Dostai says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי אֶלָּא בִּבְכוֹר בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: Ben Azzai said this only regarding a firstborn alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the back-and-forth about רב נחמן and turns to study the ברייתא that was quoted during that discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל בַּה׳" includes קדשים קלים (רבי יוסי הגלילי) or שלמים (בן עזאי), and according to אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי, בן עזאי meant only a בכור.

steps.title: What does בן עזאי come to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes בן עזאי's view and asks what his narrower wording, "to include שלמים," is meant to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: בן עזאי says: to include שלמים. What does that come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins analyzing בן עזאי's opinion and is setting up the next move by asking what he meant to leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי named only שלמים, not all קדשים קלים the way רבי יוסי הגלילי did. If he included only שלמים, he must be excluding some other kind of offering, and the גמרא wants to know which one. Steps 5 and 6 answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude what?

phrases.english: The Master said: Ben Azzai says:
to include peace-offerings.
To exclude what?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַשְּׁלָמִים. לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Zooms in on בן עזאי's opinion from the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which offering בן עזאי means to exclude by mentioning only שלמים.

steps.title: Suggesting that בן עזאי meant to exclude בכור, and rejecting it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that בן עזאי's narrow wording leaves out בכור. It rejects this with a קל וחומר: if even שלמים count as the owner's property, a בכור obviously counts as the כהן's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say בן עזאי meant to exclude a בכור, that cannot be right. Think about it: שלמים need סמיכה, נסכים and the waving of the breast and thigh, and still you say they belong to their owners. Do we even need to say that a בכור belongs to its owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a possible answer to the question from Step 4: maybe בן עזאי's wording leaves out בכור. It knocks that answer down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים carry many signs of holiness: the owner leans his hands on it, it comes with נסכים, and its breast and thigh are waved. Even so, בן עזאי calls them the owner's property. A בכור has none of these things, so it should belong to its owner even more. בן עזאי would not need to say anything special about it, so his wording cannot be meant to leave it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before it is brought as a קרבן
Wine and flour offerings that are brought along with certain קרבנות
Waving the breast and the thigh of the animal
The owners' property
'Is it even needed?' This means the case is too obvious to need saying

phrases.english: If you say: to exclude a firstborn,
now, if peace-offerings,
which require leaning of hands and libations
and waving of the breast and thigh,
you say it is the owners' property;
is it even necessary to say this about a firstborn?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לְמַעוֹטֵי בְּכוֹר, הַשְׁתָּא וּמָה שְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a first answer to Step 4's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that בן עזאי's wording is meant to leave out בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By קל וחומר from שלמים, a בכור would surely count as its owner's property, so there would be no reason to exclude it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: בן עזאי's wording leaves out מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that בן עזאי's narrow wording is meant to leave out מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: the wording is meant to exclude מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: After the בכור suggestion was rejected, רבי יוחנן gives the real answer: בן עזאי is leaving out מעשר בהמה, so he holds that it is not the owner's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying only 'שלמים,' בן עזאי keeps מעשר from being counted as the owner's property. The next step brings a ברייתא to show why מעשר is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Every tenth animal of one's flock, which becomes holy and is brought as a קרבן
Rather. It signals that the earlier suggestion is dropped and a new answer is coming

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yochanan said:
it is to exclude animal tithe,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְמַעוֹטֵי מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after Step 5 rejected the בכור suggestion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What בן עזאי's narrow wording 'to include שלמים' leaves out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It leaves out מעשר בהמה, which בן עזאי does not treat as the owner's property.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that מעשר can never be sold, unlike a בכור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא contrasts בכור and מעשר. A בכור may be sold in certain situations, but מעשר may never be sold in any situation. This shows that מעשר is not treated as the owner's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: about a בכור the תורה says 'you shall not redeem,' yet it may be sold alive if it has no blemish, and alive or slaughtered if it has a blemish. About מעשר the תורה says 'it shall not be redeemed,' and it may not be sold at all: not alive, not slaughtered, not without a blemish, and not with a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן. It shows why מעשר is treated differently from a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being able to sell something is a sign that it is yours. A בכור can be sold in some cases, so it acts like its owner's property. מעשר can never be sold, so it does not act like property, and that is why בן עזאי leaves it out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught.' This introduces a ברייתא as support
'You shall not redeem,' said about a בכור
'It shall not be redeemed,' said about מעשר
An animal without a blemish
An animal with a blemish

steps.confusionAlert: Both פסוקים forbid redeeming the animal, so they sound alike. The difference is about selling: a בכור may be sold in some cases, but מעשר never may.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
About a firstborn it is said: "You shall not redeem,"
and it may be sold: if unblemished, while alive;
and if blemished, alive or slaughtered.
About tithe it is said: "It shall not be redeemed,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ נִמְכָּר לֹא חַי וְלֹא שָׁחוּט,
phrases.english: and it may not be sold, neither alive nor slaughtered,
neither unblemished nor blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר is not the owner's property, so בן עזאי's wording leaves it out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a בכור may be sold in some cases, while מעשר may never be sold in any case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear contrast: a בכור acts like property because it can be sold, and מעשר does not because it can never be sold.

steps.title: רבינא's version: the question is asked on אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי's words
steps.stepSummary: רבינא places the question on the last part of the ברייתא instead. אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says בן עזאי meant only a בכור, and the גמרא asks what that is meant to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא teaches this discussion on the last part of the ברייתא: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says, 'בן עזאי said this only about a בכור.' What is that meant to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second version of the discussion, taught by רבינא. It sets up the question again, this time on אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי's words, and steps 9 and 10 answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the question was about בן עזאי's own words, 'to include שלמים.' In רבינא's version, the question is about אבא יוסי's words, 'only about a בכור': which other קרבן does that narrow phrase leave out?

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a ברייתא or משנה
Only
What?

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not adding a new point after רבי יוחנן's answer. He is giving another version of the same discussion, attached to a different line of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Ravina teaches it on the last clause:
phrases.notes: He asks the same question on the end of the ברייתא, אבא יוסי's words, instead of on בן עזאי's words.

phrases.english: Abba Yosei ben Dostai says:
Ben Azzai did not say this
except about a firstborn alone.
To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the discussion from Steps 4 to 7, now attached to the end of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי's narrow phrase 'only about a בכור' is meant to leave out.

steps.title: Only a firstborn cannot mean to leave out peace-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'only בכור' leaves out שלמים. It rejects this with a קל וחומר: if a בכור, holy from the womb, still counts as property, then שלמים certainly do.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the wording is meant to leave out peace-offerings, that cannot be right. A firstborn is holy from the moment it is born, and it still counts as its owner's property. So obviously peace-offerings count as property too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible answer to the question from step 8 and throws it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור becomes holy by itself at birth, and it still counts as the כהן's property. שלמים were a person's own animal before he made them holy, so they should count as his property even more. Because of that, 'only בכור' cannot be meant to leave out שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the גמרא offers a possible answer, usually to reject it)
Holy from the womb, meaning holy automatically from birth
His property
Is it even a question? (meaning: obviously)

phrases.english: If you say: it is to leave out peace-offerings,
Now, if a firstborn,
which is holy from the womb,
is still his property,
phrases.notes: 'His' here means the כהן who receives the בכור.

phrases.english: do we even need to ask about peace-offerings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers one possible answer to step 8's question and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that 'only בכור' leaves out שלמים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קל וחומר shows שלמים are even more clearly property than a בכור

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it leaves out animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the narrow wording is meant to leave out מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is meant to leave out the animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the answer: the animal that does not count as property is מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שלמים ruled out, רבי יוחנן points to מעשר as the type of קדשים that does not count as the owner's property. The next step brings the source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: מעשר בהמה, the tenth animal of the flock, which is made holy

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is to leave out the tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 9 rejected שלמים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the narrow wording leave out?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows tithe can never be sold
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a בכור may be sold in certain situations, but מעשר may never be sold. This supports the idea that מעשר is not the owner's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: about a firstborn the תורה says 'you shall not redeem,' and it may be sold unblemished while alive, or blemished while alive or after slaughter. About tithe the תורה says 'it shall not be redeemed,' and it may not be sold at all: not alive and not slaughtered, not unblemished and not blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being allowed to sell something shows that you own it. A בכור can be sold in some situations, so it counts as property. מעשר can never be sold, so it does not count as the owner's property, just as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Unblemished
An animal with a blemish
Slaughtered
It shall not be redeemed

phrases.english: As it is taught: about a firstborn it says 'You shall not redeem,'
and it may be sold when unblemished, while alive,
and when blemished, alive or slaughtered;
about tithe it says 'It shall not be redeemed,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ נִמְכָּר לֹא חַי וְלֹא שָׁחוּט,
phrases.english: and it may not be sold, not alive and not slaughtered,
not unblemished and not blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer
steps.raayaObject: מעשר is not the owner's property
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting the sale of בכור and מעשר

steps.title: But he said only a firstborn: left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי said 'only בכור,' which seems to leave out everything else, including שלמים. This does not fit רבי יוחנן's answer, and the גמרא admits the difficulty: קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'only a firstborn'! This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer from the exact wording, and then admits it has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'only' (בלבד) sounds as if nothing besides a בכור counts as property, not even שלמים. But the קל וחומר and רבי יוחנן's answer both treat שלמים as property, leaving out only מעשר. The גמרא cannot solve this, so it ends with קשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: Only
It is difficult (a challenge left unanswered)

steps.whatToRemember: In רבינא's version, the word 'only בכור' cannot be fully explained. Leaving out מעשר makes sense, but the word 'only' seems to leave out שלמים too, so the גמרא ends with קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: Here קשיא means the גמרא admits it has no answer. It does not mean the halacha is decided against this view.

phrases.english: But he said 'only a firstborn'!
phrases.notes: 'He' is אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי, from step 8.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer from the word 'only' and leaves it unanswered
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the wording leaves out only מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Only בכור' implies that even שלמים are left out, which goes against the קל וחומר and the claim that only מעשר is left out

steps.title: רבא: The phrase means ordinary, non-holy property
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'נכסים שאין בהן מעילה' means property that is not subject to the laws of מעילה at all, which is the property of an ordinary person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does 'property that has no מעילה' mean? It means property that has no law of מעילה at all. And what is that? Property of an ordinary person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and brings רבא's different way of reading its phrase "property that has no מעילה," in place of the earlier reading that tied it to קדשים קלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the phrase was read as pointing to certain holy animals that still count as the owner's property. רבא reads it more simply: it means anything with no connection to the laws of מעילה at all. That leaves only ordinary, non-holy property, and so all הקדש is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin of using holy (הקדש) property for ordinary purposes
The law or category of מעילה, meaning being subject to those rules at all
An ordinary person, as opposed to the Temple or הקדש
'They are', used to ask what something refers to

phrases.english: Rava said:
What does 'property that has no misuse' mean?
It means property that has no law of misuse at all.
And what is that? Property of an ordinary person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מַאי ״נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן מְעִילָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the ברייתא and returns to the משנה, giving an alternative to the earlier reading that the phrase refers to קדשים קלים (per רבי יוסי הגלילי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase refers to holy animals that still count as the owner's property
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase simply means ordinary property of a הדיוט, with no holiness at all
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "נכסים שאין בהן מעילה" means property with no connection to the laws of מעילה at all, which is the property of a הדיוט.

steps.title: Then the משנה should just say 'ordinary property'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: if the משנה means ordinary property, why not say 'of a הדיוט' plainly? The גמרא admits this is a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it teach 'of an ordinary person'! This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reading because the משנה used a roundabout phrase instead of the simple word 'הדיוט'. It admits it has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה only meant non-holy property, the clear way to say it would be 'property of a הדיוט'. Choosing the phrase about מעילה suggests something more specific was meant. The גמרא leaves this as an unanswered difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Then let it teach', a challenge asking why the text did not say it differently
'It is difficult', meaning the challenge stays unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא here does not mean רבא's view is fully rejected in law. It means the wording problem remains unanswered.

phrases.english: But let it teach 'of an ordinary person'!
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that the phrase means ordinary property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the meaning, the משנה would have used the simpler word 'הדיוט' instead of a phrase about מעילה.

steps.title: רבי אבא: Damages from שלמים come from the meat, not the altar parts
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that when שלמים cause damage, the injured party collects from their meat but not from their אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: שלמים that caused damage: he collects from their meat, but he does not collect from their sacrificial parts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אבא gives a ruling about collecting payment when a שלמים animal causes damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים are partly eaten by the owners (the meat) and partly burned on the מזבח (the אימורין). רבי אבא says the injured party may collect only from the meat portion. The אימורין are not available for payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offerings, a type of קדשים קלים whose meat is eaten by the owners
Caused damage
Collects payment
Their meat, the part eaten by the owners
The parts of an offering burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Peace-offerings that caused damage:
he collects from their meat,
but he does not collect from their sacrificial parts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about damage involving holy animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damages caused by שלמים are collected from the meat, not from the אימורין.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious? The altar parts go up to God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אבא needed to say this, since the אימורין obviously belong on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! The sacrificial parts go up to the One Above!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא's ruling as too obvious to need saying. It is setting up an explanation of what he really meant to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows the אימורין are burned on the מזבח, so of course a damaged person cannot take them. The גמרא asks what new point רבי אבא is adding. The answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is obvious', a challenge asking why a statement was needed
'To the One Above', meaning to God, to the מזבח
Go up, are offered

phrases.english: It is obvious!
The sacrificial parts go up to the One Above!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבא's ruling as stating something obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's ruling that one does not collect from the אימורין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the אימורין are given to the מזבח, they clearly cannot be used to pay damages, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The meat does not cover the share of the sacrificial parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אבא's ruling is needed. It teaches that the injured party cannot collect from the meat the portion of the damages that matches the אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed: to teach that he cannot collect from their meat the amount that corresponds to the sacrificial parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16 by showing that רבי אבא taught something new. You cannot collect from the meat to make up for the share that belongs to the אימורין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows the אימורין themselves go on the מזבח and cannot be taken. The new point is about the meat. One might think the injured party can take extra from the meat to make up for the אימורין's share. רבי אבא says no: the owner pays only according to his own share of the animal, which is the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (for the obvious case); it is needed for a different case. This phrase introduces a new point.
To collect payment
From their meat (the part the owner eats)
Corresponding to, matching the share of

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as just repeating 'he can't take the אימורין.' The point is that he also can't take extra meat to make up for the אימורין's share.

phrases.english: No, it is needed:
to teach that one does not collect from their meat the amount corresponding to the sacrificial parts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why say the obvious' challenge of step 16 by giving רבי אבא's ruling a new meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of scope: the ruling is about collecting from the meat in place of the אימורין, not about the אימורין themselves.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא only told us that the אימורין themselves cannot be taken, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אבא teaches that the meat cannot be used to make up for the share of the damages that matches the אימורין.

steps.title: Which opinion does רבי אבא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא's view רבי אבא's ruling matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks which side of a known מחלוקת רבי אבא's ruling follows, and then it will test each option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new explanation of רבי אבא is a question of collecting from one source when another source cannot pay. That matches the מחלוקת between רבנן and רבי נתן. The גמרא is about to show a problem with each side.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Which opinion does this follow?
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: According to whom?
phrases.notes: This refers to the case of an ox that pushed an animal into a pit, where רבנן and רבי נתן argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 17 by placing it inside a known תנאים dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אבא's ruling follows רבנן or רבי נתן.

steps.title: According to רבנן, the ruling is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אבא follows רבנן, his ruling is obvious. רבנן already hold that money you can't collect from one source cannot be collected from another.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבנן, it is obvious! Don't they say that whenever payment can't be collected from this one, it is not collected from that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and finds it makes רבי אבא's ruling unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן teach a general rule: if one source cannot pay, you cannot shift that loss onto another source. The אימורין cannot pay, so of course the meat does not cover their share. רבי אבא would be telling us nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?
But they already say
To be paid, to collect payment
From this one

phrases.english: If according to the Rabbis, it is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרִי כִּי לֵיכָּא לְאִשְׁתַּלּוֹמֵי מֵהַאי,
phrases.english: Don't they say: when it cannot be collected from this one,
phrases.notes: In the pit case, 'this one' is the ox owner and 'that one' is the pit owner.

phrases.english: it is not collected from that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First side of the question of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 17 that רבי אבא's ruling teaches something new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבנן's general rule, not covering the אימורין's share from the meat is already known, so the ruling is unnecessary.

steps.title: According to רבי נתן, the ruling seems wrong
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אבא follows רבי נתן, his ruling seems to contradict him. רבי נתן holds that money you can't collect from one source is collected from another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it follows רבי נתן, doesn't he say that whenever payment can't be collected from this one, it is collected from that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option and finds that רבי אבא's ruling goes against it. That leaves the ruling stuck on both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן says that if one source cannot pay, the loss can be shifted to the other source. By that logic, the injured party should collect the אימורין's share from the meat. That is the very opposite of what רבי אבא ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: And if
But he says
It is paid, it is collected

steps.whyThisMatters: This completes a two-sided challenge. Under רבנן the ruling is not needed, and under רבי נתן it seems wrong. The גמרא will need to find a way out of this.

phrases.english: And if according to Rabbi Natan,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר: כִּי לֵיכָּא לְאִשְׁתַּלּוֹמֵי מֵהַאי,
phrases.english: doesn't he say: when it cannot be collected from this one,
it is collected from that one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי נָתָן הָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second side of the question of step 18, completing the two-sided challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's ruling as explained in step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נתן's principle would let the injured party collect the אימורין's share from the meat, which goes against רבי אבא.

steps.title: רבי אבא's ruling can fit either side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אבא's ruling can match either רבי נתן or רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it follows רבי נתן; if you want, say it follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short headline answer to both problems from steps 19-20. It is setting up the next two steps, which explain each option in detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the ruling looks obvious according to רבנן. Step 20 said it looks contradictory according to רבי נתן. Here the גמרא claims both problems can be solved, and it explains how in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say; introduces one of several possible answers
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: If you wish, say: it follows Rabbi Natan,
if you wish, say: it follows the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי נָתָן, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of steps 19-20 with a headline answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dual-path answer: the ruling works under both views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא's ruling is either unnecessary (רבנן) or contradicted (רבי נתן).
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling fits both opinions, as the next steps explain.

steps.title: According to רבנן: one body is different from two
steps.stepSummary: רבנן's rule might have applied only when two bodies (like an ox and a pit) cause the damage. With one body, the injured party might have collected from any part, so רבי אבא had to teach otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it follows רבנן: their rule only applies with two bodies. But with one body, the injured party can say: 'I will collect from wherever I want.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אבא's ruling is not obvious, even according to רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן said you cannot collect from the pit owner what you couldn't collect from the ox owner. That case involves two separate bodies. Here only one animal did the damage, so one might think the injured party can collect the whole amount from the meat. רבי אבא teaches that he cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only; this rule is limited to
Two bodies; two separate things that caused the damage
One body; a single thing that caused the damage
I will collect payment

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבנן changed their opinion here. The גמרא is only explaining what someone might have mistakenly thought, which is why רבי אבא needed to say his ruling.

phrases.english: If you wish, say it follows the Rabbis –
that rule applies only with two bodies,
phrases.notes: Two bodies means the ox that pushed and the pit it fell into.

phrases.english: but with one body
phrases.notes: One body means the single consecrated animal: its meat goes to the owner, and its אימורין go on the מזבח.

phrases.english: he can say to him:
"From anywhere I want, I will collect."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבָּנַן – הָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּתְרֵי גוּפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of step 21's answer, the רבנן option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (one body vs. two bodies)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one body, the injured party could collect the full damage from the meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אבא teaches that even with one body, the אימורין's share cannot be collected from the meat.

steps.title: According to רבי נתן: the pit owner is a separate responsible party
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן's rule applies only in the ox-and-pit case, where the ox owner can tell the pit owner: 'I found my ox in your pit, so whatever I can't collect from the other one, I collect from you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it follows רבי נתן: only there can the owner of the ox say to the owner of the pit, 'I found my ox in your pit. Whatever I cannot collect from that one, I will collect from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אבא's ruling does not contradict רבי נתן. It does this by limiting רבי נתן's rule to the pit case, setting up a contrast with our case of one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן's reasoning depends on the pit owner being a separate party who is responsible in his own right: the ox was found in his pit. In רבי אבא's case there is no second responsible party to turn to, so רבי נתן's rule doesn't apply.

keyTerms.meaning: There; in that other case
The owner of the ox (here, the ox that was damaged)
The owner of the pit
From that other one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא's ruling fits both views. For רבנן, it teaches that even one body doesn't allow collecting from anywhere. For רבי נתן, collecting from another source only works when there is a second separate party responsible, like the pit owner.

phrases.english: If you wish, say it follows Rabbi Natan –
it is there that he can say to him,
the owner of the ox to the owner of the pit:
"I found my ox in your pit;
whatever I cannot collect from that one –
phrases.notes: "That one" is the owner of the ox that pushed my ox into the pit.

phrases.english: I will collect from you."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי נָתָן – הָתָם הוּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּעַל שׁוֹר לְבַעַל הַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of step 21's answer, the רבי נתן option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבי נתן's rule to its original case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי נתן's rule would let the injured party collect the אימורין's share from the meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי נתן's rule depends on the pit owner's own responsibility, which is missing in רבי אבא's case.
